purpose: The four REQUIRED DGO_HTTPFlowRegistry columns that need a person, with what can be proposed from evidence and what cannot. Proposals are kept out of the seed on purpose.

columns.whatItIs: The business or technical system a flow belongs to.
columns.howProposed: From the estate's own naming convention, one rule per prefix, each stated. A flow matching no rule gets no proposal.

columns.whatItIs: How much depends on this flow working.
columns.howProposed: From wiring, never from name: a flow a contract key calls is High because the platform cannot serve that key without it; a flow touching five or more lists with no key is Medium. Anything else is left for a person.

columns.whatItIs: Who is accountable for this flow.
columns.howProposed: Not proposable. Nothing in a repository knows who owns a flow, and an invented address is worse than an empty column because a flow with a plausible owner stops being chased.

columns.whatItIs: When the flow was last observed running.
columns.howProposed: Not a decision at all — an observation. No person can supply it and no repository holds it; it is written by the first registration that reads run history, or by the flow itself.
